subject: math
title: Grade 8 Surface Area and Volume of Prisms and Cylinders
seo_title: Grade 8 Surface Area and Volume Worksheets: Prisms and Cylinders (Free, Answer Key, BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Surface area and volume of regular solids, including triangular and other right prisms and cylinders
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 math worksheets on surface area and volume for the BC curriculum: volume of rectangular and triangular prisms, cylinders with V = πr²h (π ≈ 3.14), surface area from nets, the Pythagorean theorem for missing sides, and word problems with tents, cans, rain barrels and fish tanks. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Volume = area of base × height. Surface area = the area of the whole net.
key_sub: Use the radius, not the diameter, and r² means r × r. A cylinder net is 2 circles and a rectangle as long as the circumference. Volume is in cm³, surface area in cm².
body_html:
Volume: area of base × height

Volume is the space inside a solid, in cubic units (cm³, m³). A right prism is a stack of layers shaped like its base, so for every right prism V = area of base × height. Find the area of the base first, then multiply.

Cylinders

A cylinder is like a prism with a circle for a base. The area of the circle is π × r², so V = π × r² × h. Use π ≈ 3.14. The radius r goes from the centre to the edge; it is half the diameter.

Example 1

A can has a diameter of 8 cm and a height of 12 cm. What is its volume?

r = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm. V = 3.14 × 4 × 4 × 12 = 50.24 × 12.

Answer: 602.88 cm³

Surface area of a prism

Surface area is the total area of all the faces, in square units (cm², m²). Unfold the solid into a net and add the areas of every face. A box has 6 rectangles. A triangular prism has 2 triangles and 3 rectangles.

If a side of a right triangle is missing, find it with the Pythagorean theorem: c² = a² + b².

Example 2

A triangular prism is 10 cm long. Its ends are right triangles with legs of 6 cm and 8 cm. What is its surface area?

Third side: √(6² + 8²) = √100 = 10 cm. Two triangles: 2 × ½ × 6 × 8 = 48. Three rectangles: (6 + 8 + 10) × 10 = 240. SA = 48 + 240.

Answer: 288 cm²

Surface area of a cylinder

A cylinder unfolds into 2 circles and a rectangle. The rectangle is as long as the circumference (2 × π × r) and as tall as the cylinder. So SA = 2 × π × r² + 2 × π × r × h.

Volume and capacity

Capacity is how much a container can hold. 1 cm³ holds exactly 1 mL.

VolumeCapacity
1 cm³1 mL
1000 cm³ (a 10 cm cube)1 L
1 m³1000 L

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the diameter as rHalve the diameter first: d = 8, r = 4
r² as r × 2r² = r × r: 4² = 16, not 8
Writing cm² for a volume or cm³ for an areaVolume: cm³, m³. Surface area: cm², m²
Forgetting ½ for a triangle baseTriangle area = ½ × b × h
Using the sloped side as the height of a triangleUse the height that meets the base at a right angle
Counting only one circle or only the faces you can seeAdd every face of the net: a cylinder has 2 circles

faq.q: What do Grade 8 students learn about surface area and volume in BC?
faq.a: The BC Grade 8 curriculum covers the surface area and volume of right prisms (including triangular prisms) and cylinders. Students use nets for surface area and V = area of base × height for volume.

faq.q: How do you find the surface area of a cylinder?
faq.a: Add the two circles and the rectangle from the net: SA = 2 × π × r² + 2 × π × r × h. For r = 3 cm and h = 10 cm (π ≈ 3.14): 56.52 + 188.4 = 244.92 cm².

faq.q: Why do I need the Pythagorean theorem for surface area?
faq.a: A triangular prism has a rectangle on each side of the triangle. If one side of a right triangle is not given, find it with c² = a² + b² before you add the rectangles.

faq.q: What is the difference between surface area and volume?
faq.a: Surface area is the area that covers the outside of a solid, in square units like cm². Volume is the space inside, in cubic units like cm³, and 1 cm³ holds 1 mL.

sets.title: Volume of rectangular and triangular prisms

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: Area of the base: 8 × 5 = 40 cm². V = area of base × height = 40 × 9 = 360 cm³. Multiply (do not add), and write cubic units for a volume.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: Area of the base: 9 × 8 = 72 cm². V = area of base × height = 72 × 6 = 432 cm³. Multiply (do not add), and write cubic units for a volume.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: Area of the base: 7 × 5 = 35 cm². V = area of base × height = 35 × 11 = 385 cm³. Multiply (do not add), and write cubic units for a volume.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: Area of the base: 5 × 4 = 20 m². V = area of base × height = 20 × 3 = 60 m³. Multiply (do not add), and write cubic units for a volume.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: Area of the base: 9 × 7 = 63 cm². V = area of base × height = 63 × 11 = 693 cm³. Multiply (do not add), and write cubic units for a volume.

items.q: A rectangular prism is 3.5 cm long, 4 cm wide and 2 cm high. What is its volume?
items.e: V = 3.5 × 4 × 2 = 14 × 2 = 28 cm³. Count the decimal places to check your answer.

items.q: A rectangular prism is 1.2 m long, 0.5 m wide and 2 m high. What is its volume?
items.e: V = 1.2 × 0.5 × 2 = 0.6 × 2 = 1.2 m³. Count the decimal places to check your answer.

items.q: A cube has edges that are 2.5 cm long. What is its volume?
items.e: V = 2.5 × 2.5 × 2.5 = 6.25 × 2.5 = 15.625 cm³. 7.5 adds the three edges, and 6.25 is the area of one face.

items.q: The ends of this prism are right triangles. What is its volume?
items.e: Base (the triangle): ½ × 8 × 6 = 24 cm². V = 24 × 15 = 360 cm³. Without the ½ you get 720, a whole box, twice too big.

items.q: The ends of this prism are right triangles. What is its volume?
items.e: Base (the triangle): ½ × 5 × 12 = 30 cm². V = 30 × 10 = 300 cm³. Without the ½ you get 600, a whole box, twice too big.

items.q: The ends of this prism are right triangles. What is its volume?
items.e: Base (the triangle): ½ × 9 × 4 = 18 cm². V = 18 × 11 = 198 cm³. Without the ½ you get 396, a whole box, twice too big.

items.q: The ends of this prism are right triangles. What is its volume?
items.e: Base (the triangle): ½ × 7 × 6 = 21 cm². V = 21 × 16 = 336 cm³. Without the ½ you get 672, a whole box, twice too big.

items.q: The ends of this prism are right triangles. What is its volume?
items.e: Base (the triangle): ½ × 10 × 5 = 25 cm². V = 25 × 14 = 350 cm³. Without the ½ you get 700, a whole box, twice too big.

items.q: Each end of a prism is this triangle. The prism is 10 cm long. What is its volume?
items.e: Use the height (the dashed line), not the sloped side. Base: ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 cm². V = 12 × 10 = 120 cm³. Using the 5 cm sloped side gives 150.

items.q: Each end of a prism is this triangle. The prism is 9 cm long. What is its volume?
items.e: Use the height (the dashed line), not the sloped side. Base: ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 cm². V = 48 × 9 = 432 cm³. Using the 10 cm sloped side gives 540.

items.q: Each end of a prism is this triangle. The prism is 12 cm long. What is its volume?
items.e: Use the height (the dashed line), not the sloped side. Base: ½ × 16 × 6 = 48 cm². V = 48 × 12 = 576 cm³. Using the 10 cm sloped side gives 960.

items.q: Which formula gives the volume of any right prism?
items.e: A prism is a stack of layers the same shape as its base. V = area of base × height. For a box, the base area is l × w, so V = l × w × h.

items.q: The volume of this rectangular prism is 540 cm³. What is its height?
items.e: Area of the base: 12 × 5 = 60 cm². Height = 540 ÷ 60 = 9 cm. Check: 12 × 5 × 9 = 540. 45 divides by 12 only, and 480 subtracts.

items.q: A triangular prism has a volume of 360 cm³. Each end is a triangle with a base of 8 cm and a height of 6 cm. How long is the prism?
items.e: Area of the triangle: ½ × 8 × 6 = 24 cm². Length = 360 ÷ 24 = 15 cm. 7.5 cm forgets the ½ (360 ÷ 48).

items.q: The base of a prism is a trapezoid with parallel sides of 5 cm and 9 cm and a height of 4 cm. The prism is 12 cm long. What is its volume?
items.e: Area of the trapezoid = (5 + 9) ÷ 2 × 4 = 28 cm². V = 28 × 12 = 336 cm³. Forgetting to divide by 2 gives 672.

items.q: What is the volume of this cylinder? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: 10 cm goes all the way across the top, so it is the diameter. r = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm. V = 3.14 × 5 × 5 × 6 = 78.5 × 6 = 471 cm³. Using 10 as r gives 1884, 4 times too big.

items.q: What is the volume of this cylinder? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: 16 cm goes all the way across the top, so it is the diameter. r = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm. V = 3.14 × 8 × 8 × 5 = 200.96 × 5 = 1004.8 cm³. Using 16 as r gives 4019.2, 4 times too big.

items.q: What is the volume of this cylinder? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: 8 cm goes all the way across the top, so it is the diameter. r = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm. V = 3.14 × 4 × 4 × 7 = 50.24 × 7 = 351.68 cm³. Using 8 as r gives 1406.72, 4 times too big.

items.q: What is the volume of this cylinder? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: 18 cm goes all the way across the top, so it is the diameter. r = 18 ÷ 2 = 9 cm. V = 3.14 × 9 × 9 × 6 = 254.34 × 6 = 1526.04 cm³. Using 18 as r gives 6104.16, 4 times too big.

The volume of this cylinder is 628 cm³. What is its height? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: Base: 3.14 × 5 × 5 = 78.5 cm². Then 78.5 × h = 628, so h = 628 ÷ 78.5 = 8 cm. 40 cm divides by 3.14 × 5 (r, not r²).

items.q: Cylinder A has a radius of 4 cm and a height of 10 cm. Cylinder B has a radius of 8 cm and a height of 5 cm. Which statement is true? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
c: B holds 4 times as much as A
A holds twice as much as B
B holds twice as much as A
items.e: A: 3.14 × 4 × 4 × 10 = 502.4 cm³. B: 3.14 × 8 × 8 × 5 = 1004.8 cm³. Doubling r makes r² 4 times bigger, and halving h cuts that in half, so B holds twice as much.

sets.title: Surface area of prisms from nets

items.q: Which shapes make the net of a triangular prism?
items.e: A triangular prism has a triangle at each end and a rectangle for each of the 3 sides of the triangle: 2 triangles and 3 rectangles.

items.q: Liam finds the surface area of a box. Which unit should his answer have?
items.e: Surface area is an area (the paper that covers the box), so it is in square units: cm². cm³ and mL are for volume, and cm is for length.

items.q: This is the net of a rectangular prism. What is its surface area?
items.e: Top and bottom: 2 × (7 × 3) = 42. Front and back: 2 × (7 × 5) = 70. Ends: 2 × (3 × 5) = 30. SA = 42 + 70 + 30 = 142 cm². Add all 6 faces.

items.q: This is the net of a rectangular prism. What is its surface area?
items.e: Top and bottom: 2 × (9 × 4) = 72. Front and back: 2 × (9 × 6) = 108. Ends: 2 × (4 × 6) = 48. SA = 72 + 108 + 48 = 228 cm². Add all 6 faces.

items.q: This is the net of a rectangular prism. What is its surface area?
items.e: Top and bottom: 2 × (8 × 5) = 80. Front and back: 2 × (8 × 4) = 64. Ends: 2 × (5 × 4) = 40. SA = 80 + 64 + 40 = 184 cm². Add all 6 faces.

items.q: This is the net of a rectangular prism. What is its surface area?
items.e: Top and bottom: 2 × (12 × 4) = 96. Front and back: 2 × (12 × 3) = 72. Ends: 2 × (4 × 3) = 24. SA = 96 + 72 + 24 = 192 m². Add all 6 faces.

items.q: This is the net of a rectangular prism. What is its surface area?
items.e: Top and bottom: 2 × (6 × 2) = 24. Front and back: 2 × (6 × 8) = 96. Ends: 2 × (2 × 8) = 32. SA = 24 + 96 + 32 = 152 cm². Add all 6 faces.

items.q: This is the net of a cube. What is its surface area?
items.e: One square: 4 × 4 = 16 cm². A cube has 6 equal faces: 6 × 16 = 96 cm². 64 cm³ is the volume, and 48 counts only 3 faces.

items.q: A cube has a surface area of 150 cm². How long is each edge?
items.e: 6 equal faces: 150 ÷ 6 = 25 cm² for one face. 5 × 5 = 25, so each edge is 5 cm. 25 is the area of a face, not an edge.

items.q: What is the surface area of this rectangular prism?
items.e: Top and bottom: 2 × (5 × 4) = 40. Front and back: 2 × (5 × 3) = 30. Ends: 2 × (4 × 3) = 24. SA = 40 + 30 + 24 = 94 cm². 47 counts only the 3 faces you can see; the hidden faces count too.

items.q: A box is 10 cm long, 6 cm wide and 4 cm high. What is its surface area?
items.e: Top and bottom: 2 × (10 × 6) = 120. Front and back: 2 × (10 × 4) = 80. Ends: 2 × (6 × 4) = 48. SA = 120 + 80 + 48 = 248 cm². 240 is the volume (10 × 6 × 4), and 360 uses the largest face 6 times.

items.q: An open tray (no top) is 10 cm long, 8 cm wide and 5 cm high. What is its outside surface area?
items.e: Bottom: 10 × 8 = 80. Two long sides: 2 × 10 × 5 = 100. Two ends: 2 × 8 × 5 = 80. SA = 80 + 100 + 80 = 260 cm². 340 includes a top the tray does not have, and 180 leaves out the bottom.

items.q: This is the net of a triangular prism. What is its surface area?
items.e: Two triangles: 2 × ½ × 6 × 8 = 48. Three rectangles: (6 + 8 + 10) × 15 = 24 × 15 = 360. SA = 48 + 360 = 408 cm².

items.q: This is the net of a triangular prism. What is its surface area?
This is the net of a triangular prism. What is its surface area?
items.e: Two triangles: 2 × ½ × 5 × 12 = 60. Three rectangles: (5 + 12 + 13) × 8 = 30 × 8 = 240. SA = 60 + 240 = 300 cm².

items.q: This is the net of a triangular prism. What is its surface area?
This is the net of a triangular prism. What is its surface area?
The ends of a triangular prism are right triangles with legs of 5 cm and 12 cm. How long is the third side of each triangle?
items.e: Use the Pythagorean theorem: c² = 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169. c = √169 = 13 cm. 17 adds the legs, and 169 forgets the square root.

items.q: Each end of a prism is an isosceles triangle with a base of 16 cm and a height of 15 cm. How long is each sloped side?
items.e: The height cuts the base in half, making a right triangle with legs of 8 cm and 15 cm. c² = 8² + 15² = 64 + 225 = 289, so c = √289 = 17 cm. 23 adds 8 + 15, 31 adds 16 + 15, and 289 forgets the square root.

items.q: The ends of this prism are right triangles. Find the sloped side with the Pythagorean theorem, then find the surface area.
items.e: Sloped side: √(6² + 8²) = √100 = 10 cm. Two triangles: 2 × ½ × 6 × 8 = 48. Three rectangles: (6 + 8 + 10) × 12 = 288. SA = 48 + 288 = 336 cm². 216 leaves out the sloped rectangle, 384 forgets the ½, and 288 cm³ is the volume.

items.q: Which shapes make the net of a cylinder?
items.e: A cylinder has a circle on the top, a circle on the bottom, and a curved side. The curved side unrolls into a rectangle, so the net is 2 circles and 1 rectangle.

items.q: In the net of a cylinder, the long side of the rectangle is the same length as …
items.e: The rectangle wraps once around the circle, so its long side is the circumference, 2 × π × r.

items.q: A cylinder has a radius of 6 cm. In its net, how long is the rectangle? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: The rectangle is as long as the circumference: 2 × 3.14 × 6 = 37.68 cm. 18.84 forgets the 2, 113.04 is the area of the circle, and 75.36 uses 12 cm (the diameter) as r.
Two circles: 2 × 3.14 × 1.5 × 1.5 = 14.13. The rectangle is as long as the circumference: 2 × 3.14 × 1.5 = 9.42, so its area is 9.42 × 6 = 56.52. SA = 14.13 + 56.52 = 70.65 cm².
Two circles: 2 × 3.14 × 5 × 5 = 157. The rectangle is as long as the circumference: 2 × 3.14 × 5 = 31.4, so its area is 31.4 × 6 = 188.4. SA = 157 + 188.4 = 345.4 cm².
Two circles: 2 × 3.14 × 3 × 3 = 56.52. The rectangle is as long as the circumference: 2 × 3.14 × 3 = 18.84, so its area is 18.84 × 7 = 131.88. SA = 56.52 + 131.88 = 188.4 cm².
Two circles: 2 × 3.14 × 4 × 4 = 100.48. The rectangle is as long as the circumference: 2 × 3.14 × 4 = 25.12, so its area is 25.12 × 5 = 125.6. SA = 100.48 + 125.6 = 226.08 cm².
Two circles: 2 × 3.14 × 6 × 6 = 226.08. The rectangle is as long as the circumference: 2 × 3.14 × 6 = 37.68, so its area is 37.68 × 10 = 376.8. SA = 226.08 + 376.8 = 602.88 cm².

The 8 cm line goes all the way across the circle, so it is the diameter: r = 4 cm. Two circles: 2 × 3.14 × 4 × 4 = 100.48. The rectangle is as long as the circumference: 2 × 3.14 × 4 = 25.12, so its area is 25.12 × 9 = 226.08. SA = 100.48 + 226.08 = 326.56 cm².

The 10 cm line goes all the way across the circle, so it is the diameter: r = 5 cm. Two circles: 2 × 3.14 × 5 × 5 = 157. The rectangle is as long as the circumference: 2 × 3.14 × 5 = 31.4, so its area is 31.4 × 3 = 94.2. SA = 157 + 94.2 = 251.2 cm².

items.q: What is the surface area of this cylinder? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: Two circles: 2 × 3.14 × 3 × 3 = 56.52. The rectangle is as long as the circumference: 2 × 3.14 × 3 = 18.84, so its area is 18.84 × 8 = 150.72. SA = 56.52 + 150.72 = 207.24 cm². A closed cylinder has two circles, top and bottom.

items.q: What is the surface area of this cylinder? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: Two circles: 2 × 3.14 × 7 × 7 = 307.72. The rectangle is as long as the circumference: 2 × 3.14 × 7 = 43.96, so its area is 43.96 × 5 = 219.8. SA = 307.72 + 219.8 = 527.52 cm². A closed cylinder has two circles, top and bottom.

items.q: What is the surface area of this cylinder? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: 12 cm is the diameter, so r = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm. Two circles: 2 × 3.14 × 6 × 6 = 226.08. The rectangle is as long as the circumference: 2 × 3.14 × 6 = 37.68, so its area is 37.68 × 5 = 188.4. SA = 226.08 + 188.4 = 414.48 cm².

items.q: What is the surface area of this cylinder? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: 4 cm is the diameter, so r = 4 ÷ 2 = 2 cm. Two circles: 2 × 3.14 × 2 × 2 = 25.12. The rectangle is as long as the circumference: 2 × 3.14 × 2 = 12.56, so its area is 12.56 × 10 = 125.6. SA = 25.12 + 125.6 = 150.72 cm².

items.q: A cylinder has a radius of 5 cm and a height of 12 cm. What is the area of its curved side only? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: The curved side is the rectangle in the net: circumference × height = (2 × 3.14 × 5) × 12 = 31.4 × 12 = 376.8 cm². 188.4 forgets the 2, 533.8 adds the two circles, and 942 cm³ is the volume.

items.q: A cup is a cylinder with no top. Its radius is 4 cm and its height is 9 cm. What is its outside surface area? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: Bottom: 3.14 × 4 × 4 = 50.24. Curved side: 2 × 3.14 × 4 × 9 = 226.08. SA = 50.24 + 226.08 = 276.32 cm². 326.56 counts a top the cup does not have.

items.q: A cylinder has a radius of 1.5 m and a height of 4 m. What is its surface area? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: Two circles: 2 × 3.14 × 1.5 × 1.5 = 14.13. Curved side: 2 × 3.14 × 1.5 × 4 = 37.68. SA = 14.13 + 37.68 = 51.81 m². 44.745 counts one circle, and 131.88 uses 3 m (the diameter) as r.
Rectangle: 31.4 × 8 = 251.2 cm². Two circles: 2 × 3.14 × 5 × 5 = 157 cm². SA = 251.2 + 157 = 408.2 cm². 251.2 is only the rectangle, and 329.7 counts one circle.

items.q: Which expression gives the surface area of a cylinder with a radius of 3 cm and a height of 10 cm?
items.e: Surface area = two circles + the rectangle = 2 × π × r² + 2 × π × r × h = 2 × 3.14 × 3 × 3 + 2 × 3.14 × 3 × 10 = 56.52 + 188.4 = 244.92 cm². 3.14 × 3 × 3 × 10 is the volume.

items.q: Which has the greater surface area: a cylinder with a radius of 5 cm and a height of 10 cm, or a cube with 10 cm edges? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)

sets.title: Surface area and volume word problems

items.q: A juice box is 6.5 cm long, 4 cm wide and 10 cm high. How much juice can it hold?
items.e: V = 6.5 × 4 × 10 = 26 × 10 = 260 cm³. 1 cm³ holds 1 mL, so it holds 260 mL. (2.6 L would be 2600 mL, and 20.5 adds the edges.)

items.q: Mei’s fish tank is 50 cm long, 25 cm wide and 30 cm high. How many litres does it hold when full?
An aquarium has a base 60 cm long and 30 cm wide. Ethan pours in 36 L of water. How deep is the water?
items.e: 36 L = 36 000 cm³. Base area: 60 × 30 = 1800 cm². Depth = 36 000 ÷ 1800 = 20 cm. 600 divides by the length only.

items.q: Hana builds a cedar planter box that is 100 cm long, 40 cm wide and 30 cm deep inside. Soil comes in 25 L bags. How many bags does she need to fill the box?
items.e: V = 100 × 40 × 30 = 120 000 cm³ = 120 L. 120 ÷ 25 = 4.8, so 4 bags are not enough. She needs 5 bags.

items.q: Ava wraps a gift box that is 25 cm long, 20 cm wide and 8 cm high. What is the least amount of wrapping paper that covers the whole box?
items.e: Top and bottom: 2 × 25 × 20 = 1000. Front and back: 2 × 25 × 8 = 400. Ends: 2 × 20 × 8 = 320. SA = 1000 + 400 + 320 = 1720 cm². 4000 is the volume number, and 860 counts only 3 faces.

items.q: A paper label wraps once around the curved side of a soup can. The can has a radius of 4 cm and a height of 11 cm. What is the area of the label? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: The label is the rectangle in the net: (2 × 3.14 × 4) × 11 = 25.12 × 11 = 276.32 cm². The label does not cover the top or bottom, so 376.8 is too much. 138.16 forgets the 2.

items.q: A tin of BC salmon is a cylinder with a radius of 4 cm and a height of 3.5 cm. About how much does it hold? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: V = 3.14 × 4 × 4 × 3.5 = 50.24 × 3.5 = 175.84 cm³. 1 cm³ = 1 mL, so it holds about 176 mL. 703 uses the diameter (8 cm) as r, and 88 uses r × 2 instead of r × r.

items.q: Noah’s tent at a campsite near Whistler is a triangular prism 3 m long. Each end is a triangle with a base of 2.4 m, a height of 1.6 m and sloped sides of 2 m. How much nylon covers the whole tent, including the floor?
items.e: Two triangle ends: 2 × ½ × 2.4 × 1.6 = 3.84. Three rectangles: (2 + 2 + 2.4) × 3 = 6.4 × 3 = 19.2. SA = 3.84 + 19.2 = 23.04 m². 26.88 forgets the ½, and 19.2 leaves out the ends.

items.q: How much space is inside Noah’s tent? (Each end is a triangle with a base of 2.4 m, a height of 1.6 m and sloped sides of 2 m. The tent is 3 m long.)
items.e: Area of the end: ½ × 2.4 × 1.6 = 1.92 m². V = 1.92 × 3 = 5.76 m³. 7.2 uses the sloped side instead of the height, 11.52 forgets the ½, and 1.92 is only the end.

items.q: A rain barrel in Vancouver is a cylinder with a diameter of 50 cm and a height of 80 cm. How many litres of rain can it hold? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
A water tank in an Okanagan orchard is a cylinder with a radius of 1 m and a height of 2.5 m. Kai paints the curved side and the top, but not the bottom. What area does he paint? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: Curved side: 2 × 3.14 × 1 × 2.5 = 15.7. Top: 3.14 × 1 × 1 = 3.14. Total: 15.7 + 3.14 = 18.84 m². 21.98 also paints the bottom, and 7.85 m³ is the volume.

items.q: A backyard pool in Kelowna is 9 m long and 4 m wide. The water is 1.5 m deep everywhere. How many litres of water are in the pool?
A hose fills the same 54 000 L pool at 30 L per minute. How many hours does it take to fill?
items.e: 54 000 ÷ 30 = 1800 minutes. 60 minutes = 1 hour, so 1800 ÷ 60 = 30 hours. 1800 is the number of minutes, not hours.

items.q: Container A is a cylinder with a radius of 5 cm and a height of 10 cm. Container B is a box 9 cm × 9 cm × 10 cm. Which holds more, and by how much? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
A concrete footing for a deck in Surrey is a cylinder with a diameter of 30 cm and a depth of 120 cm. How many litres of concrete fill it? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
A cardboard poster tube is a closed cylinder with a radius of 4 cm and a length of 60 cm. How much cardboard is needed to make it, including both ends? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: Two ends: 2 × 3.14 × 4 × 4 = 100.48. Curved side: 2 × 3.14 × 4 × 60 = 1507.2. SA = 100.48 + 1507.2 = 1607.68 cm². 1557.44 counts one end, and 3416.32 uses 8 cm (the diameter) as r.

items.q: A round tank at a salmon hatchery on Vancouver Island has a radius of 2 m. The water in it is 1 m deep. How many litres of water are in the tank? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: V = 3.14 × 2 × 2 × 1 = 12.56 m³. 1 m³ = 1000 L, so 12.56 × 1000 = 12 560 L. 50 240 L uses the diameter (4 m) as r, and 6280 L uses r instead of r × r.

items.q: A box is 10 cm long, 6 cm wide and 4 cm high. Arjun makes a new box with every edge twice as long. How many times greater is the volume of the new box?
items.e: Old: 10 × 6 × 4 = 240 cm³. New: 20 × 12 × 8 = 1920 cm³. 1920 ÷ 240 = 8. Each of the three edges doubles, so the volume is 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 times greater.

items.q: For the same two boxes (10 cm × 6 cm × 4 cm and 20 cm × 12 cm × 8 cm), how many times greater is the surface area of the new box?
items.e: Old SA: 2 × (60 + 40 + 24) = 248 cm². New SA: 2 × (240 + 160 + 96) = 992 cm². 992 ÷ 248 = 4. Each face is 2 times as long and 2 times as wide, so its area is 2 × 2 = 4 times greater.

items.q: Olivia makes an open-top storage bin for her classroom from plastic sheet. The bin is 30 cm long, 20 cm wide and 15 cm high. How much plastic does she need?
items.e: Bottom: 30 × 20 = 600. Long sides: 2 × 30 × 15 = 900. Ends: 2 × 20 × 15 = 600. Total: 600 + 900 + 600 = 2100 cm². 2700 adds a lid the bin does not have, and 9000 is the volume number. 1350 counts only one of each face.
